title: Aggregation: $project, $sort, $skip and $limit
summary: Shape pipeline output by choosing fields, calculating new ones, sorting and trimming the results.

quiz.q: You want the 3 cheapest products. Which stage order is right?
quiz.explain: Sort from smallest to largest first, then keep the first three. Limiting first would pick three arbitrary products and sort only those.

quiz.q: Complete the stage so the output holds only the `name` field and no `_id`.
quiz.explain: `$project` selects and shapes the fields of each output document.

quiz.q: The collection holds prices 30, 10, 20 and 40 in that order. What does the pipeline return? Type the prices separated by spaces.
quiz.explain: Sorted: 10, 20, 30, 40. Skipping 1 leaves 20, 30, 40. Limiting to 2 leaves 20 and 30.

quiz.q: In `{ $project: { total: { $add: ['$price', '$tax'] } } }`, what does the `$` in `'$price'` mean?
options: It is a pattern for a regular expression
It reads the value of the field price from the current document
It marks the last item of an array
quiz.explain: Inside an expression a string starting with `$` is a field path. Without it, `'price'` would be plain text.

exercise.task:
Using the `products` collection (fields `name`, `category`, `price`), write a pipeline that:

- keeps only products in the `'gadget'` category
- sorts them by `price`, highest first
- skips the most expensive one, then keeps the next **2**
- outputs only `name`, `price`, and a new field `priceWithDelivery` equal to `price + 50` (no `_id`)
hints: Write five stages in this order: `$match`, `$sort`, `$skip`, `$limit`, `$project`.
The new field is `priceWithDelivery: { $add: ['$price', 50] }`. Set `_id: 0` to hide the id.

db.products.aggregate([
  { $match: { category: 'gadget' } },
  { $sort: { price: -1 } },
  { $skip: 1 },
  { $limit: 2 },
  { $project: { _id: 0, name: 1, price: 1, priceWithDelivery: { $add: ['$price', 50] } } }
])
